channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Candidates clash over cost of living in French presidential debate
item.description: Five of the frontrunners for the French presidential election lined up for the second of this year's debates on Monday night. In an often-rowdy debate, candidates clashed over counterproposals to raise and cut taxes and slash public spending.

item.title: Do school cellphone bans work? New study says yes – but it's complicated
item.description: A new study of school cellphone bans finds they may help students make up for some of the learning they've lost since 2013 – a divergence from earlier study results. (Image credit: Jason Ardan)

item.title: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
item.description: While the rise of AI continues to fuel the debate over whether college is worth the cost, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment, drawing in people of all backgrounds including college graduates. (Image credit: Andrew Spear for NPR)

item.title: France's far-right presidential candidate Le Pen to set out pension plans
item.description: France's far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen is to set out pension proposals on Tuesday as she seeks to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular electoral pledges ‌with promises to restore order to the public finances. Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) has pledged to allow people ⁠who started work young to retire as early as 60, although it is under pressure to detail how it would ‌do this while also curbing budget deficits.

item.title: Ukraine launches 'unprecedented' strike on Crimean bridge, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for the second consecutive night on Monday, according to Russian-aligned authorities on the occupied peninsula.

item.title: Russia receiving ‘dozens of missiles per month’ from North Korea, says Kyiv
item.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that Russia was receiving "dozens of missiles per month" from North Korea and warned that the country was taking advantage of the war to make its weapons "more effective". He called on European allies to send more weapons so that Ukraine can respond "on equal terms" to the threat.

item.title: China, Canada agree to further reduce tariffs at APEC summit in Shenzhen
item.description: China is hosting the 21-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen this week, hoping to use the tech megalopolis to showcase its vision for international trade and development. The summit is also where the international agenda is enacted: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has met with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, with both leaders agreeing to reduce trade barriers between their countries. Also in this edition: Nvidia reportedly rejects a return of its former CEO Jensen Huang.

item.title: AFCON 2027 qualifiers: Senegal beat Sudan and close in on qualification
item.description: Senegal beat Sudan 4–2 on Matchday 4 of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Senegal top Group J and could secure qualification as early as Tuesday, November 17.

item.title: Iran live updates: Bahrain reports new attack, IRGC says it targeted US radar
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Xi and Carney call for deeper ties as Canada looks beyond US for trade
item.description: The leaders of China and Canada have called for deeper ties as Ottawa navigates strained relations with the United States and seeks closer cooperation with Beijing

item.title: Live: France braces for new day of protests as unions call for nationwide strike
item.description: France braced for another day of protests Tuesday as unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises. Youth organisations and Yellow Vest activists are also set to join the demonstrations. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: TGJones put up for sale in latest high street shake-up
item.description: The high street chain which for more than two centuries traded under the WH Smith brand is being put up for sale just weeks before Christmas.

item.title: New mass protests expected in France Tuesday as presidential election approaches
item.description: Unions in France are calling for a strike Tuesday to demand wage increases, with students also expected to join. With under five months to go before the presidential election, FRANCE 24's Monte Francis asks Ariane Bogain, Senior Lecturer in French Politics at Northumbria University, what role the widespread discontent will play in the upcoming vote.

item.title: ICE agents accused of throwing pregnant US citizen to ground, pepper-spraying her
item.description: A pregnant U.S. citizen was allegedly pepper-sprayed and thrown to the ground on her stomach before being arrested, video shared by her attorney appears to show.

item.title: Three Melbourne Cup trophies worth £500k each stolen
item.description: Police are searching for three Melbourne Cup trophies collectively worth more than £1.5m after they were stolen from a display cabinet at a racecourse in Melbourne.

item.title: Macron visits Malaysia as France seeks closer defence, rare earths ties
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron met Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday to discuss strengthening defence, trade, energy and critical minerals cooperation. Macron's two-day visit, his first since 2017, comes ahead of the countries' 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations, with both sides seeking a strategic partnership.

item.title: Trump in Asia for historic nuclear talks with China and Russia
item.description: US President Donald Trump landed in Asia on Monday for economic talks and a planned trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on nuclear issues and the war in Ukraine. Trump also raised the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit.

item.title: The advice Biden got from Mitt Romney, and other takeaways from his memoir
item.description: Biden's memoir "Promise Me, America," which drops Tuesday, recounts his 2020 run for the presidency, his years in the White House and his tumultuous 2024 run.

item.title: Snow warning in place for parts of UK this morning
item.description: A yellow alert for snow is in force for parts of the UK, with forecasters warning of possible travel disruption.

item.title: France Cricket federation faces collapse after funding scandal exposed by FRANCE 24
item.description: France's national cricket organisation is on the verge of collapse, a top administrator says, three years after an explosive FRANCE 24 investigation revealed accusations that the body was faking matches to claim funds from the International Cricket Council.

item.title: Live: Ukrainian drone, missile strikes damage key Crimea Bridge
item.description: Ukrainian drone strikes on Tuesday damaged sections of the Crimea Bridge in the second day of attacks on key infrastructure in the Russian-occupied territory. Russian strikes in Kyiv also hit two bridges overnight from Monday, causing closures and knocking out heating and water in Kyiv. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Russian strikes hit two key bridges in Kyiv, disrupting water and power supplies
item.description: Russian forces struck two major bridges crossing the Dnipro River in Kyiv late Monday, damaging critical infrastructure and causing water and power cuts in parts of the Ukrainian capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The attacks came as Moscow launched a wider wave of drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, including in the regions of Cherkasy and Kharkiv.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo leaves Peru after historic 12-day South America trip
item.description: Pope Leo departed Peru on Monday concluding an emotional 12-day trip to South America as he recovers from cancer surgery. ABC News’ Melissa Adan reports.

item.title: WATCH: NYC teen builds candle business with refillable cement containers
item.description: What started as helping his sister make candles for a birthday party at age 13 has turned into a thriving business for New York City teen Christon Lennon.

item.title: WATCH: Meet the rental car manager going viral for keeping customers calm during ground stop
item.description: Perley Provost, manager of Enterprise Rent-A-Car at Denver International Airport, shares how he kept stranded passengers calm and hydrated during Friday's widespread ground stop.

item.title: Americans urged to 'keep a low profile' in UK amid terror threat over festive season
item.description: US citizens in the UK have been warned to "keep a low profile" and remain vigilant to potential terror attacks during the festive period.

item.title: Ukraine hits key Crimea bridge with drones
item.description: "I think the Ukrainians are trying to send a message to the Russians with this - 'If you hit our bridges we can hit yours,'" reports Gulliver Cragg from Kyiv.

item.title: WATCH: Trump blames Biden administration for FAA ground stop & other stories
item.description: Nationwide FAA ground stop resulted from equipment failure, says administrator; Anthropic to price its IPO this week; NOAA reports strong El Niño expected to peak in the New Year

item.title: Chase outage disrupts US online banking, Zelle payments
item.description: Users of several major US banking apps and online portals reported outages on Monday, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.com, with one institution ruling out a cyberattack as the cause. Among those affected by the outages were Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and the popular money transfer app Zelle.

item.title: La Francophonie 'waning in global influence': Linguistic institutions becoming 'less important'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Phil Clark, professor of international politics at SOAS University of London. The diplomatic crisis between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo spilling out at the Francophonie summit in Phnom Penh for all to see has exposed an unexpected shift in their relations. Clark says that "nobody expected Rwanda to back down in this way" following President Macron's request that Paul Kagame withdraw Louise Mushikiwabo's candidacy for a third term.

item.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence
item.description: As Europe's ​defence ministries look to limit dependency on American technology and major software company Palantir Technologies for critical military functions, a growing number of firms within the region are competing for their business. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Arthur Holland Michel, journalist and researcher specialising in emerging military technologies.

item.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
item.description: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices. (Image credit: California Department of Justice)

item.title: Trump says he needs funding for air traffic control after ground stop
item.description: US ​President ​Donald Trump, pressed on a ​technology ‌failure ⁠that ‌grounded thousands of ⁠flights last week, ​on ‌Monday told reporters ‌that ​the government needed funding for upgrade ​to ​air traffic ​control equipment. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Sheldon Jacobson, Professor of Computer Science at the University of Illinois. He explains that "the Republicans have had full control of the House and the Senate since the President came in. They controlled everything. If they needed the money and wanted the money they could have approved the money. The fact that they didn't, in the the different bills that have been passed, suggests that it's more than just money that is going on here".

item.title: Trump blames ground stop on old tech that had 'heart attack'
item.description: Friday's ground stop resulted in thousands of cancelled flights.

item.title: Rogue AI: California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face and other cyberattacks
item.description: The US state of California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI over the Hugging Face incident and other cyberattacks, accusing the ChatGPT maker of knowingly testing dangerous advanced AI models without adequate safeguards. Meanwhile, the US Commerce Department has tightened rules over the export of US technology, aiming to close a loophole around remote access to advanced AI chips.

item.title: US judge strikes down Trump visa restrictions on foreign students, journalists
item.description: A US federal judge struck down a Trump administration policy on Monday that would have sharply limited the length of time foreign students and journalists could stay in the country, ruling that the proposed restrictions were unlawful and would undermine educational opportunity.

item.title: Rwanda to host hub for rejected EU migrants
item.description: In tonight's edition, five European countries are negotiating a deal to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. Also, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda's political animosity spills over at the Francophonie Summit in Cambodia. And in Tunisia, young women are increasingly turning towards weightlifting and bodybuilding as a form of self-expression.

item.title: November 17 blackout hoax: How a conspiracy theory went viral around the world
item.description: A conspiracy theory claiming a worldwide “blackout” will hit on November 17 has spread across social media, cutting electricity, internet and banking services. The rumour stems from a routine US FEMA emergency alert test, but was amplified by cryptocurrency accounts, misleading claims about EU preparedness advice and references to The Simpsons. Recent technology outages, flight disruptions and cyberattacks have added to public anxiety, helping turn a routine test into a global blackout hoax.

item.title: Pope concludes South America homecoming, reassures faithful after cancer scare
item.description: Pope Leo XIV finished Monday his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru reiterating his advocacy for social justice, environmental protection and the importance of community. Just a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery, the 71-year-old pontiff drew millions of faithful across South America, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.

item.title: The new faces of the US Congress
item.description: The United States Congress is about to welcome dozens of new faces. A majority of them, Democratic, after the "blue wave" in the midterm elections. FRANCE 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson catches up with one of these new lawmakers as they go through orientation as they prepare to take office in January. He speaks with Katy Padilla Stout, U.S. Representative-elect for Texas's 23rd congressional district.

item.title: Trump says he 'would not mind' if Jensen Huang is reinstated as Nvidia CEO
item.description: President Donald Trump said Monday morning that he "would not mind" if Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia.

item.title: Supreme Court rebuffs Trump administration appeal over DEI funding cuts
item.description: The Supreme Court has rejected a Trump administration appeal on DEI funding cuts to academic research

item.title: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
item.description: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China. (Image credit: Taryn Ng)

item.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
item.description: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing. (Image credit: Omer Urer)

item.title: The 'crayon test' and the wrong plastic: Read this before buying your next olive oil
item.description: Olive oil has become a kitchen staple in the UK - but how many of us actually know what we're looking for?

item.title: Trump says he may meet with North Korea's Kim Jong Un during China trip
item.description: Trump's trip comes amid the Nvidia CEO scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: WATCH: Grammy nominees for Album of the Year, Song of the Year
item.description: Here are the nominees for Album of the Year and Song of the Year at the 2027 Grammys.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing
item.description: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children. (Image credit: Greg Derr)

item.title: WATCH: Who are the nominees for the 2027 Grammys?
item.description: ABC News' Chris Connelly breaks down the nominees for the 69th Grammy Awards with Raye leading the field with 11 nominations.

item.title: Retrial date set for Lindsay Clancy over killing of her three children
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is due to face a retrial next March over the killing of her three young children.

item.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino faces challenge from French football chief
item.description: The head of the French Football Federation (FFF) will stand against Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election, UEFA have revealed.

item.title: WATCH: New video of tanker collision and riverboat sinking
item.description: Authorities say a 500-foot Atlantic asphalt tanker collided into the American Heritage cruise ship on Friday, causing the ship to fall on its side and capsize in just 22 minutes.

item.title: US to further curb China's access to Nvidia chips
item.description: The US government is set to further restrict China's access to the most powerful AI chips, such as the ones provided by tech giant Nvidia.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: 'Cat Tour' brings together cat lovers in Massachusetts
item.description: ABC News' Danny New explains how feline lovers recently got their fix in Somerville, Massachusetts.

item.title: At least 17 people killed in two separate shootings in South Africa
item.description: At least 17 people have been killed in two separate shootings in South Africa, police said on Monday.

item.title: William and Kate land in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize trip
item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales have arrived ‌in Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize awards, ‌marking the couple's first official trip overseas in nearly four years.

item.title: WATCH: Passenger jet collides with UPS plane on taxiway at Miami International Airport
item.description: A UPS cargo plane and a Copa Airlines passenger jet collided on a taxiway at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, according to airport officials and the FAA.

item.title: Van Hollen says Schumer's team trying to 'instill fear' to retain Senate leadership
item.description: Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen touted his chances of becoming Senate majority leader when Democrats take control of the Senate in January.

item.title: Company caught up in Nvidia controversy launches internal investigation
item.description: A cloud computing company facing scrutiny over claims involving tech giant Nvidia has launched an internal investigation conducted by external lawyers.

item.title: WATCH: World Sanfilippo Awareness Day
item.description: This global campaign brings public awareness and attention to Sanfilippo Syndrome, a rare, terminal genetic disorder that causes dementia in children for which there is currently no cure.

item.title: WATCH: Skylar's big surprise by the New England Patriots
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Skylar, a pediatric cancer patient, got an extra surprise from New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye while spending a day baking with Ann Michael Maye.

item.title: WATCH: Elementary school named after beloved custodian
item.description: Marilyn Hampton was a beloved custodian for the Aubrey Independent School District outside Dallas, Texas. She was surprised with a school named in her honor, Marilyn Hampton Elementary School.

item.title: Lauren Boebert will lose her seat in Congress to Democrat Laubacher, AP projects
item.description: Colorado Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert will lose her House seat to Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher, The Associated Press projected Friday.

item.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders receives 2028 presidential encouragement
item.description: Supporters and donors have been encouraging GOP Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders to run for president in the 2028 cycle, sources told ABC News.
